title: Predicting knee pain severity in professional distance runners using gaussian process regression
summary: 50 professional runners aged 20–30, self-reported continuous symptom score (not diagnosed injury), 70/30 holdout with train-only 5-fold tuning. Results: held-out MSE .020, RMSE .144, MAE .116, R2 .475 versus mean baseline MSE .047. Small single-cohort sample.
ai_technology: Gaussian process regression predicts self-reported symptom severity; primary Results explicitly say this is symptom monitoring, not injury diagnosis
